instructor: Even though the instructor was an expert on the field, I think my impressions was generally negative. I think the instructor didn't fully read the assignment that she gave notes. As an example, in our midterm assignment I wrote 14 sentences that said ".... was the aim of the exhibition" in a 5-6 pages. The instructor criticized me like "then what is the aim? you didn't mention". The similar issue was the same for Review assignments too. Even though I clearly explained and literally wrote the sentence, the instructor criticized me like "why didn't you explain". I appriciate and respect the instructor's background and works and definetly support her but this is the situation and I wanted to take critiques which are valid and didn't already exist in a written text.
course: The course and the content was quite good. But it can and should develop. The guest lecturers should be welcomed and a final colloborated outcome can be produced. course:
En olumlu tarafı: Power point sunuları eşliğinde, okumalar yüzeysel de olsa açıklandı. 
En olumsuz tarafı: Ders ne yazık ki lisans dersi düzeyinde kaldı. Dersin ileriye doğru giden, öğrenciyi geliştiren bir yapısı olmadığını, daireler çizerek aynı soruları tekrar ettiğini söylemek zorundayım.
I understand that it is a graduate course and the academic side is more intense, but it is not suitable for this type of course where everything is purely theory and we do nothing practically.

I think the problem is there is a lot of workloads even for an MA-level course. Each and every assignment required at least 2000 thousand words of written research. Even though being an elective course, this class was the heaviest course for me. The lectures are also not very sufficient, they are not giving you enough knowledge of how to prepare a proposal for a curatorial exhibition. For instance, she doesn't teach how to write an introductory text but asks you to write one in one of her assignments. Grading criteria is also not very transparent. She asks you to include things in your written research that you already have included and gives you lower grades for reasons that are not justified.

The course is nothing more than an average under-grad course. I felt like the balance between the theoretical and practical work of the course was off. Maybe it can be improved by choosing either one aspect to be either properly theoretical or practical. This way, the course content feels a little unrelated to the workload expected.

course:
I was really interested in most of the subjects we discussed but I was not a fan of the excessive background information we had to study along with it.  We went over the first and second world wars from the starting point like 5 times. I don't remember studying both wars this much even in high school. 
Also, as far as I'm concerned this is a theory class so, I did not understand why we had to be in breakout rooms every lecture. I get that it should be interactive regardless but I was really bored out of my mind when we had to search for something in the middle of the class and not present it. Because the format did not work. There were at least 5 or 6 rooms and almost every answer was the same. So only 2 groups got to talk and the others just sat silently. It didn't work. Some people were absent as well making the others in the rooms struggle. 

This was also the first time I had a midterm where we had to answer 25 or more questions in small essay format, in 1 and a half hours.  My grade is one of the highest in the class but I still struggled because it was just too much. I think the course wants to give too much information in too little time. Relax a bit, I can guarantee you that with this amount of knowledge all of us studied enough to pass the exams and not enough to actually learn. The subjects were interesting but most of us were lost when we had to study the history of  Russian Politics. 

The presentations. If we are going to have reflections every two weeks and a midterm and a final on top of that why the presentation? I wish it counted as the final instead.
the course teaches a lot about the history of graphic design but I think this teaching should be more than memorization.
